questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following two statements :

I. if $n$ is a composite number, then n divides $\left(n - 1\right) !

II. There are infinitely many natural numbers $n$ such that $n^{3} + 2n^{2} + n$ divides~$n !$.

Then

$
options: I is true and II is false
I is false and II is true
questions.solution:
If $n$ is a composite number (Take $n = 4$)

For $n = 4, n$ does not divide $\left(n - 1\right)$!

Hence $Ist$ statement is false

(II) $n^{3} + 2n^{2} + n = n\left(n + 1\right)^{2}

$n $\left(n + 1\right)^{2}$ divides $n !

If $n$ is such that \left(n + 1\right) is a prime number (Take $n = 6$) so $n$\left(n + 1\right)^{2}$ does not divide $n !$ but there are infinite values of $n \left(=104, 109, 114, \ldots\right) for which $n$\left(n + 1\right)^{2}$ divide $n !$& but it is not true for every natural numbers.
